items.prompt:
Read the story below.

A rabbit and a turtle decided to race. The rabbit ran very fast and got far ahead. He stopped to rest under a tree. The turtle kept walking slowly and steadily. The turtle crossed the finish line while the rabbit was still sleeping. The turtle won the race.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that slow and steady effort can win over speed when someone gets overconfident and stops trying.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara saw a classmate eating lunch alone every day. She finally walked over and sat with him. They talked and laughed for the whole lunch period. The next day the boy smiled when he saw Amara coming. They became good friends.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that a small act of kindness, like sitting with someone who is alone, can lead to a real friendship.

items.prompt:
Read the fable below.

A boy was watching a flock of sheep. To have fun, he shouted, "Wolf! Wolf!" The farmers ran out to help, but there was no wolf. He did it again the next day, and they came running again. One day a real wolf came. The boy shouted for help, but no one came. They did not believe him anymore.

What is the central message of this fable?
items.answer: The central message is that if you lie, people will stop trusting you, and no one will believe you when you are telling the truth.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo left his bicycle outside every night. One morning it was very rusty and the chain broke. His dad said, "Things you care about need to be taken care of." Leo cleaned the bike, fixed the chain, and kept it inside from then on.

What lesson did Leo learn?
items.answer: Leo learned that you need to take care of the things you value or they will get damaged.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia found a shiny coin on the playground. She picked it up and put it in her pocket. All day she wondered if it belonged to someone. At the end of the day she gave it to her teacher to put in the lost-and-found box. She felt much better after that.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that doing the honest thing, even when it is hard, makes you feel better in the end.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James wanted to bake cookies all by himself. He followed the recipe but left them in the oven too long and they burned. The next time he baked, he set a timer. The cookies came out perfectly. Everyone in his family wanted to try one.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that making a mistake is part of learning, and you can do better the next time if you pay attention to what went wrong.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia's little brother was afraid of the dark. Every night he crawled into her room and woke her up. Nadia felt annoyed at first. Then she remembered being afraid of the dark herself when she was little. She put a small night light in his room. He stopped being afraid.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that understanding how someone else feels can help you show kindness instead of annoyance.

items.prompt:
Read the fable below.

A mother eagle taught her chicks to fly by pushing them out of the nest one by one. Each chick was frightened at first but soon discovered that their wings worked perfectly. By the end of the day every chick was soaring high above the trees.

What is the central message of this fable?
items.answer: The central message is that you often have to face your fears to discover what you are capable of.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Owen worked very hard on a drawing for the school art show. When he finished, he asked his older sister what she thought. She said it was nice but the sky looked empty. Owen added clouds and a bird. He liked it much better. "Good advice makes good art better," his sister said.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that being open to helpful feedback makes your work better.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara and her friend argued about which game to play at recess. Neither would give in. They ended up sitting on the bench the whole time and did not play anything. The next day they took turns choosing the game and had so much fun they did not want to stop.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that sharing and taking turns is better than arguing, because everyone ends up having more fun.

items.prompt:
Read the fable below.

A wind and a sun made a bet about who could make a traveler remove his coat. The wind blew as hard as it could, but the traveler pulled his coat tighter. Then the sun shone gently and warmly. The traveler soon took off his coat and sat down to rest in the sunshine.

What is the central message of this fable?
items.answer: The central message is that gentleness and warmth are more powerful than force.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo's soccer team lost three games in a row. Some players wanted to quit. Their coach said, "Every loss shows us what to practice." They worked on their weak spots every afternoon. In their next game, they won by two goals.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that losing can teach you what to improve, and hard work after a loss can lead to success.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia's neighbor planted sunflowers along the fence every spring. Sofia asked why she went to all that trouble. The neighbor said, "Because every time I see them, I feel happy, and so do all the people who walk by." Sofia planted sunflowers in her own yard the next spring.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that creating beauty in your own space can bring joy to yourself and to others.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James told his friend a secret he had been asked to keep. The friend told others, and soon everyone knew. The person who had shared the secret with James was hurt and stopped trusting him. James learned a hard lesson about keeping promises.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that breaking a promise hurts people who trusted you and destroys the trust they had in you.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia was afraid to sing in front of her class. Her teacher said she did not have to, but Nadia decided to try anyway. Her voice shook at first, but she kept going. When she finished, the class clapped and her teacher smiled. Nadia felt taller than she ever had.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that doing something brave, even when you are afraid, can give you a great sense of pride and confidence.
